boundary_decision.rationale: WM-ACT-039 correctly identifies as aggregate: owns bounded recruitment-process identity and lineage, mandatory profile, lifecycle, orchestrates external entities (Position, Vacancy, Person, Candidate, Application, Assessment, Interview, Offer, Contract, Employment) while preserving their independent ownership and identity, maintains typed neighbor relations with documented source support, and enforces non-cascading composition semantics. The frozen registry classification 'standalone-mm' refers to the record plane, not the subject model entry kind; schema enum 'aggregate' is the most defensible alternative within the required kinds (entity, event, relationship, mixin, pattern, registry, classifier, aggregate).

decisions.rationale: The model owns recruitment-process identity, design release, lifecycle state transitions (draft, authorized, open, paused, closed, filled, cancelled, corrected, superseded, archived), requisition and criterion bindings, posting versions, sourcing campaign references, process-scoped candidate-case links, stage orchestration, evidence and decision records, offer versioning, and closure lineage. This satisfies aggregate semantics: a bounded root with identity, lineage, composition relations, and governed lifecycle. The mandatory profile pattern supports single-vacancy, pooled, internal, contingent, agency, public-sector, and cross-border variants with shared orchestration semantics.

The model explicitly separates process ownership from external master ownership: process owns orchestration, evidence binding, and lifecycle assertions; Position, Vacancy, Person, Candidate, Application, Competency, Assessment, Interview, Offer, Contract, Employment remain external masters with independent authority and correction history. Non-cascading deletion rules, purpose-bound access controls, and minimum-tombstone preservation prevent master-lifecycle transfer and maintain audit evidence. Five documented neighbor boundaries (Position/Vacancy, Person/Candidate, Assessment/Interview, Recommendation/Decision/Offer, Contract/Employment) with source refs (SRC-001, 004, 012) are sound.

All 16 sources are first-party official materials for their respective standards, laws, frameworks or guidance. ISO 30405 is available here only through its public catalogue abstract, HR Open downloads require registration or terms acceptance, and ICO recruitment guidance remains draft after consultation closed. EEOC and OPM are United States and United States federal sources, while GDPR, EDPB guidance and the AI Act are European Union sources. WCAG coverage describes the digital accessibility baseline but does not prove implementation conformance. Accept for reviewable draft with source-access, regional and interoperability holds.

decisions.concept: Composition relations and external master mappings
decisions.rationale: The model correctly identifies five neighbor boundaries with source support but states 'No approved relation rows were supplied. The registry parent link to Vacancy / Matching and proposed organization, person, application, assessment, decision, offer, contract and employment relations remain candidate holds.' Composition-relation definitions (cardinality, optionality, temporal ordering, deletion cascade limits) must be approved and synchronized with external master models before schema merge. Proposed relations list: Organization, Unit, Position, Vacancy (as neighbors), Person, Candidate, Application, Competency, Qualification, Assessment, Interview, Evidence, Decision, Offer, Contract, Employment. Deferral gate: approved relation contract signatures.

decisions.concept: Privacy, sensitive data, and access control architecture
decisions.rationale: Default-deny access model with purpose-bound role views (hiring sponsor, manager, recruiter, assessor, decision-maker, rights steward, privacy steward, records steward). Sensitive-data compartments (health, accommodation, diversity, criminal, background) with restricted access, minimum disclosure, and deletion eligibility rules. Candidate rights routes (notice, opt-out, correction, deletion, appeal, redaction) are explicit. Redaction strategy includes candidate-identifier, contact-detail, compensation, health, diversity, assessment-content, interview-note, ranking, and rationale redaction policies. Audit logging requirement for actor, role, purpose, process scope, operation, policy, RFC 3339 time, affected fields, and source revision without unnecessary protected-data copy.

decisions.concept: Adversarial check enforcement: inference rejection rules
decisions.rationale: The model explicitly rejects five inference collapses: (1) consent inferred from application, (2) qualification inferred from résumé or single document, (3) eligibility inferred from sourcing or discovery, (4) suitability inferred from one score, offer acceptance, or opaque model, (5) fairness inferred from 80-percent ratio or single metric without statistical and practical context. These rules are actionable, prevent category collapse, and block deterministic claims. Four-fifths rule cited as US enforcement heuristic, not universal proof of discrimination. Fairness indicators include conversion, stage volumes, candidate experience, adverse-impact measures with small-sample and limitations caveats.

decisions.concept: Interoperability and schema crosswalk (Schema.org, ESCO, HR Open)
decisions.rationale: Mappings are versioned (Schema.org current, ESCO v1.2.1, HR Open unversioned-requires-download) and loss-aware: document process, vacancy, posting, occupation, skill, candidate-case, application, stage, assessment, decision, offer mappings with declared omissions, semantic conflicts, access limits, and round-trip loss. Pinned source and target versions required. No full conformance or round-trip claim made. ICO guidance is draft. Round-trip testing must validate before interoperability claim; proposed relations held for standards review.

decisions.concept: Regional scope and jurisdiction-specific legal alignment
decisions.rationale: Model cites EEOC (US) and OPM (US federal) for selection procedures and hiring reform; GDPR, EDPB, and EU AI Act (European Union only); ICO (United Kingdom draft guidance). Private, public, internal, contingent, agency, volunteer, platform, and cross-border recruitment have different authority, equality, notice, screening, record and remedy rules per jurisdiction. Protected-class definitions, affirmative-action duties, accessibility (ADA vs. Equality Act 2010 vs. EU accessibility directives), criminal checks, work authorization, automated-decision safeguards, notice, appeal, and retention vary by region. Legal review required for each operational jurisdiction before promotion from reviewable-draft.

Lifecycle records typed events for draft, authorization, opening, pause, closure, fill, cancellation, correction, supersession and archive. Each transition records actor, authority, rationale, effective and recorded times, evidence and correction lineage. Reopened or repeat relations, predecessor and successor identity and version management preserve earlier released history. These are model rules and validation obligations, not a claim that every implementation already enforces immutability technically.

decisions.concept: Quality, fairness, and adverse-impact measurement framework
decisions.rationale: Process owns stage volume, time, conversion, source-qualified process quality, candidate-experience, fairness and adverse-impact observations at process scope. Group selection rates may be computed only where lawful, and the four-fifths rule is retained as a United States enforcement heuristic rather than a universal definition or proof of discrimination. Denominators, cohort definitions, statistical and practical context, sample-size limitations and improvement actions remain explicit. Downstream job performance is outside this aggregate and must not be inferred from process metrics.

deferred_research: Detailed recruitment-profile variant invariants per form class: single-vacancy, pooled/evergreen, internal mobility, contingent, agency, public-sector, cross-border. Mandatory profile addresses shared orchestration but variants require distinct closed-world assumptions, approval authority, retention, remedy, and fairness-metric constraints per form.

Full ISO 30405:2023 normative text retrieval and normative conformance validation; HR Open schema structure, versioning discipline, and round-trip cardinality validation; ICO recruitment guidance promotion from draft to final with UK equality and data-protection specifics.

Independent occupational psychology, assessment-science, and test-validity review: criterion development methods, job-relevance documentation, predictive-validity evidence, differential-prediction analysis, adverse-impact indicators, alternative-assessment recommendations per role and jurisdiction.

Candidate-experience audit and WCAG 2.2 accessibility conformance testing: posting language and simplicity, application-process friction, assessment-alternative provision, interview accommodation, feedback timing, rejection-reason disclosure, appeal-route clarity, communication accessibility (audio/video/text/plain-language variants).
Independent external-provider review (Claude, Grok, or equivalent) after publication hold expires or owner reauthorizes. Single-provider artifact is time-bounded reviewable-draft.
